chunks: Ibn Mahbub narrated from 'Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام:
Regarding a slave who injured two men, he عليه السلام said: “He is to be divided between them if his offense encompasses his full value.”

It was said to him: “What if he injured one man at the beginning of the day and injured another at the end of the day?” He عليه السلام said: “He is between them so long as the governor has not ruled regarding the first injured person. But if the governor had ruled regarding the first injured person and handed him over to him on account of his offense, then he committed an offense after that, his offense is upon the latter.”

key_terms.بِقِيمَتِهِ: by his full value, meaning the compensable worth of the slave
key_terms.جِنَايَتُهُ: his offense or injurious act carrying legal liability
key_terms.عَبْدٍ: an enslaved person whose financial liability is being discussed
key_terms.فَدَفَعَهُ إِلَيْهِ: handed him over to the claimant as a result of the adjudicated offense
key_terms.ٱلْمَجْرُوحِ ٱلْأَوَّلِ: the first injured person in the sequence of claims
key_terms.ٱلْوَالِي: the governing authority or official who issues the legal ruling

ai.seo_question: How is liability determined when a slave injures two people at different times?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the liability of an enslaved person who injures multiple people. If the injury liability reaches his value, he is shared between the claimants; however, once the wali has ruled and transferred him to the first injured party, any later offense is attached to the later victim.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5267 - Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) was asked about a slave who injured two men.
Imam (as) said: "He is to be divided between them if his crime equals his full value."

It was asked: "What if he injured one man in the morning and another in the evening?"
Imam (as) replied: "He is to be divided between them as long as the governor has not ruled regarding the first injured person. But if the governor had already ruled and handed the slave over to the first injured party due to his injury, and then the slave committed another injury afterward, then his liability for that second injury falls upon the latter victim."
